title: Telemetry Bridge: Splunk/Datadog/Sentinel Onboarding & Adapter Checklist
content:
Purpose:
This working playbook captures the practical onboarding checklist, customer requirements template, RBAC v2 considerations, audit log schema mapping, and connector implementation notes for Splunk, Datadog, and Microsoft Sentinel exports. It is intended for security engineering, solutions engineering, and SREs who will deliver SIEM exports to customers or partners.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: outbound telemetry (audit logs, admin actions, evidence attachments) exported to customer SIEMs or their security tooling. Includes streaming (HEC/HTTP), batched uploads, and cloud-native ingestion (Event Hub, Kinesis etc.).
- Audience: eng-security, eng-servicing-runtime, solutions-engineering, customer-success SELs.

High-level customer onboarding checklist (quick):
1) Customer discovery call
   - Confirm target SIEM (Splunk, Datadog, Sentinel or other).
   - Required ingestion method (HEC, Logs API, Event Hub, SFTP).
   - Data residency / region constraints and contractual retention minimums.
2) Contract & security questionnaire
   - Minimum: TLS, customer IP allowlist, shared secret rotation cadence, PII handling.
3) RBAC & audit scope mapping
   - Which Redwood roles map to customer visibility roles (see RBAC section).
4) Schema & field mapping signoff
   - Provide sample events, map to customer ingestion fields, confirm timestamp precision.
5) Connector deployment & test
   - Test ingest of synthetic events, evidence attachments, failure modes, and rate limits.
6) Go-live and roll-out plan
   - Canary window, alerting thresholds, fallback plans for backpressure.

Customer requirements template (what to collect from customer):
- SIEM type and endpoint URL(s)
- Expected qps and burst (average per minute, max burst per minute)
- Authentication: HEC token / Datadog API key / Event Hub SAS / Certs
- Preferred compression (gzip yes/no) and content type (JSON/NDJSON)
- Expected retention / access requirements for attached evidence
- Redaction/PII rules: fields that must be redacted or hashed before export
- Incident enrichment needs: correlate to customer user IDs, teams, or account ids
- Contact points for escalation and SOC testing windows

RBAC v2 mapping considerations:
- Principle: exports must honor resource-level visibility and tenant isolation. RBAC v2 introduces scoped roles and attribute-based filters; exporter must filter events before sending.
- Role mapping matrix (example):
   - redwood-admin -> customer:full (send all admin/audit events)
   - redwood-sre -> customer:ops (send infra and runtime events, not user content)
   - redwood-support -> customer:read-only (support-level events, sanitized payloads)
- Implementation notes:
   - Exporter applies server-side filters at the request-routing layer; do not rely on client-side or downstream SIEM filtering for isolation guarantees.
   - Any export that could leak restricted fields must be blocked unless a signed consent artifact from the customer exists.

Audit log schema (canonical set for SIEM export)
- Field names (canonical) and short description:
   - event_id: unique UUID per event
   - event_time: ISO8601 UTC timestamp with ms precision
   - event_type: enum {auth, admin, resource_change, system, access, evidence_upload}
   - actor: object (actor.id, actor.type, actor.email) -- flattened as actor_id, actor_type, actor_email for export
   - target: object (target.id, target.type) -> flattened as target_id, target_type
   - action: verb string (e.g., create, update, delete, login, token_issue)
   - result: enum {success, failure, partial}
   - client_ip: source ip of actor request
   - user_agent: original UA string
   - req_id: request-trace-id for correlation with traces
   - tenancy_id: customer tenant id / org id
   - resource_diff: small diff or summary (text) for changes
   - evidence_ref: if present, an evidence attachment id (signed URL or reference)
   - severity: optional enum {info, low, medium, high}

Sample exported event (NDJSON-friendly single-line):
{"event_id":"e3f7a1a6-9c2b-4f3c-b327-1a2b3c4d5e6f","event_time":"2025-01-08T15:23:42.123Z","event_type":"admin","actor_id":"u-10234","actor_type":"user","actor_email":"security@acme.com","target_id":"model-xyz","target_type":"model","action":"update","result":"success","client_ip":"34.200.12.5","user_agent":"Redwood-SDK/1.4.2","req_id":"r-7b8c9d","tenancy_id":"org-789","resource_diff":"{\"param\":{\"old\":\"v1\",\"new\":\"v2\"}}","evidence_ref":"evidence-452"}

Evidence automation and attachment handling:
- Evidence types: logs snapshot, model weights hash, configuration snapshot, admin justification, signed audit package.
- Delivery patterns:
   - Inline small artifacts (<= 32KB): Base64-encoded and included as evidence_blob (avoid for PII heavy content).
   - Reference pattern: provide evidence_ref and a signed, time-limited URL that the customer SIEM can fetch (preferred for larger files).
- Integrity: include SHA256 hash of attachment in the event field evidence_hash and size_bytes.
- Access control: signed URLs must validate tenant scope and be short TTL (recommended 30 mins by default).

Provider-specific connector notes
1) Splunk (HEC):
   - Preferred format: NDJSON, HEC token auth, TLS required.
   - Recommended headers: Authorization: Splunk <HEC_TOKEN>, X-Redwood-Tenant: <tenant_id>
   - Batch size: default 100 events or 1MB payload, whichever first.
   - Example HEC endpoint: https://input-us1.splunk.example.com:8088/services/collector/event
   - Retry semantics: exponential backoff with jitter; if 4xx returned, surface to SRE and stop retries for 5m.
   - Splunk sourcetypes: use "redwood:audit" for admin logs, "redwood:evidence" for attachments metadata.

2) Datadog (Logs intake):
   - Ingest via Logs API v2 with API key header "DD-API-KEY".
   - Send as JSON arrays of events; include "ddsource":"redwood", "service":"redwood-inference"
   - Rate limits: ask customer for account-level quotas; implement per-tenant rate throttles.
   - Pipeline mapping: agree on attributes that map to Datadog facets (tenancy_id, actor_email, event_type).

3) Microsoft Sentinel (Event Hub / Logic Apps):
   - Preferred: forward to an Event Hub namespace in customer subscription. Support fallback via Logic App webhook if Event Hub unavailable.
   - Recommended mapping: envelop event in CloudEvent with subject=tenancy_id and time=event_time.
   - Authentication: use SAS tokens or AAD service principal with RBAC-limited access.

Schema mapping and enrichment notes:
- Timestamp precision: always send ms precision and include timezone (UTC).
- Denormalization: flatten nested actor/target fields for easier SIEM queries.
- Correlation ids: always include req_id and event_id; also include trace_id when available.
- Enrichments: when permitted, add internal severity score and rule_id to help SOC triage.

Privacy, redaction and PII controls:
- Default policy: redact high-risk PII fields before export (SSNs, full credit card numbers, raw prompt text longer than 1KB unless customer explicitly requests it).
- Redaction modes supported: remove-field, mask-keep-length, hash-with-salt (customer-provided salt possible).
- Audit of redactions: include redaction_metadata field listing rules applied (but not the removed values).

Backpressure, throttling, and SLOs:
- We expose per-tenant rate budgets. If customer ingestion declines (HTTP 429/503), we buffer up to 1 hour of events in persistent queue, then fallback to summarized events if buffer exceeds thresholds.
- Fail-open policy: never send events that violate RBAC or redaction rules even under pressure.

Testing, verification and signoff checklist:
- Send synthetic test vector (10 events) covering all event_types and evidence_ref patterns to customer endpoint.
- Verify 1:1 event mapping in SIEM with correct timestamps and tenant tagging.
- Verify that RBAC-filtered events are not present in the customer view.
- Verify evidence signed URLs download and hash matches evidence_hash.
- Run privacy scanner to detect leaked PII (automated script).

Operational runbooks (short):
- On 4xx from SIEM: alert and notify SE; pause shipments for that tenant for 5 minutes.
- On repeated 429/503: increase backoff window and create incident if > 5 minutes continuous failures.
- On redaction mismatch: block further shipments until agreement with customer.

Rollout / canary plan template:
- Stage 1 (dev): single test tenant, synthetic traffic.
- Stage 2 (pilot): 2–3 customers with low qps, one per SIEM type.
- Stage 3 (canary): 10% of production tenants across regions for 48 hours.
- Stage 4 (GA): full rollout with monitoring dashboards.

Appendix: common troubleshooting snippets
- Splunk HEC 401: check token & time drift; ask customer to validate HEC token scopes.
- Datadog 403: verify API key and subaccount forwarding; check IP allowlist.
- Sentinel Event Hub auth errors: validate SAS token time window and AAD permissions.

Notes and open questions:
- Should we support on-demand SFTP drop for customers who prefer non-API ingestion? (operational cost vs simplicity)
- Standard TTL for evidence signed URLs currently proposed at 30 minutes; customer requests for longer-lived artifacts should be handled via contract.
- Need definitive mapping between RBAC v2 attributes and customer-facing roles (work item: CON-5421).

Owner and next steps:
- Owner: Amira Chen (security eng)
- Next steps: review with solutions-eng (Priya) and infra (Diego), produce partner-ready adapter README and sample Terraform for Event Hub.
